findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The double sink across from the office area is in need of caulking. The gap between the wall and the piece of equipment is large enough to hold a pencil, therefore, the sink shall be caulked to the wall. Ensure that all stationary pieces of equipment are caulked to the wall to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
There were between 5-10 employees working at the time of the inspection. The kitchen manager was able to produce his food manager certificate and 2 other food handler certificates for other employees. Discussed that every employee that handles food and clean dishes shall have a food handler certificate. Ensure that food certificates are printed off and are available for all employees during routine visits. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine’s sanitizing temperatures were recorded between 124F-153F after at least 6 cycles. The dish machine was tested using several different measuring devices (heat puck and thermo stickers). See that the dish machine is serviced and its sanitizing temperature is at least 160F. Facility is instructed to wash, rinse, sanitize in triple sink until the machine is functioning properly. Will follow up 9/18/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Several cucumbers stored in cooler #4 were observed covered in mold. Discussed and shown to PIC and the cucumbers were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that all food items are maintained in good condition and never moldy. If food is observed moldy, be sure to never serve and discard items immediately.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine’s sanitizing temperature was recorded at 148.6F. The dish machine was run four times and the temperature remained the same. The PIC mentioned that MJ Kellner was suppose to visit the facility again to service the machine but hasn’t. PIC made a call to have a technician service the facility as soon as possible. The dish machine’s sanitizing temperature should always be recorded at least 160F to ensure effective sanitizing of food contact surfaces. Until the machine is functioning properly, the facility was instructed to sanitize dishes in triple sink using the available chemicals (bleach or quaternary ammonia).  Will follow-up on 9/15/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Cut tomatoes stored in cooler #1 were observed with an exceeded time/temperature control for safety of food. The cut tomatoes were dated August 18, 2025, which is past the required seven day time frame for cold holding. Discussed with PIC proper date marking and to never hold TCS items in house longer than seven days. The tomatoes were also observed moldy. The PIC discarded the cut tomatoes. Ensure that TCS foods prepared in house are held no longer than seven days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.

findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Leaks were observed at the plumbing under the prep sink (by handwashing sink) and under the third basin of the 3 part sink. PIC noted work orders were placed. Until repairs are done, staff have buckets under the plumbing to catch leaking wastewater. Make sure buckets are emptied daily/as needed and kept clean, as old wastewater can serve as a potential water source for pests.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in kitchen sani-bucket was observed at 50ppm. Required concentration per product label directions is 100-200ppm. Solution was prepared earlier that morning. Fresh solution was provided at 100ppm. Ensure bleach solutions are changed as needed throughout daily operations and maintained at 100-200ppm as required.
Chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.15 Wash gauge of the dish machine was observed at 140F during multiple cycles and did not move. The machine data plate shows the need for a wash temperature of 160F. The gauge was observed at 160F later when the District 186 maintenance technician came out to check the machine booster heater and verify proper heat sanitization. Maintenance and staff were asked to monitor the gauges to confirm proper function and replace any components if needed. It would appear based on observations today that intermittent function of the wash gauge is occurring.
A warewashing machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: Observed the dish machine to have a temperature of 144F. A work order was called by the manager. Ensure the dish machine temperature has a temperature of 160F to ensure dishes are sanitized properly. The 3 part sink will be used to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. 
After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use – standard contact time 30 seconds.
